title: Protocol Temephos Bioassay
author: Lara Ferrero Gomez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbstinen
materials: Procedure following to analyse the sensitivity of
the mosquito larvae to the Temephos 1%
Maintenance of the larvae in the laboratory

steps.title: Prepare Larval Feed
steps.instruction: Prepare commercial fish feed by crushing and autoclaving it.

steps.title: Feed and Maintain Larvae
steps.instruction: Feed larvae once daily and renew water through periodic washes generally every 3 days.

substeps.instruction: For first stadium larvae: add 0.003g of food per larva (0.3g per 100 larvae).
For last stage larvae: add 0.006g of food per larva (0.6g per 100 larvae).

steps.title: Set Up Bioassay Containers
steps.instruction: Prepare 9 transparent plastic containers, each with a 162 cm2 surface area and 200 ml of chlorine-free water.

substeps.instruction: Set up 3 containers with Temephos at the manufacturer's recommended dose (8 kg/ha), adjusted to the surface.
Set up 3 containers with Temephos at the dose used by health agents in Cape Verde (100 g/ton of water), set to the volume.

steps.title: Inoculate Larvae
steps.instruction: Add 40 L3 stage larvae to each replica.

substeps.instruction: Provide 0.005g of autoclaved fish food at the start of the experiment to prevent starvation.

steps.title: Control Environmental Conditions
steps.instruction: Maintain the following environmental parameters throughout the bioassay:

steps.title: Measure Water Parameters
steps.instruction: Use a multi-parameter meter to determine physical and chemical parameters of the water.

substeps.instruction: Measure pH, temperature, salinity, conductivity, and dissolved organic matter immediately after applying Temephos.
Repeat these physical-chemical measurements after the bioassay is finished.

steps.title: Evaluate Product Effectiveness
steps.instruction: Determine the total number of dead larvae 24:00 h post-treatment.

substeps.instruction: Invalidate and repeat the test if negative control mortality exceeds 20%.
Apply corrected mortality for mortalities above 5%.
